subject: Startups
title: Moore's Law
description: Learn Moore's Law in one minute.

hook.text: In 1965, Gordon Moore predicted that transistor counts on chips would double roughly every two years.

buildup.text: It sounded absurd. But for fifty years, the semiconductor industry hit that target with eerie consistency.

discovery.text: Moore's Law isn't physics—it's a self-fulfilling prophecy the entire industry organized itself around.

twist.text: Chipmakers spent billions on R&D precisely to keep the prediction alive. It became a competitive roadmap.

climax.text: Today's chips hold over 100 billion transistors. Moore's Law drove the fastest sustained innovation ever.

punchline.text: A prediction became a promise an entire industry kept.

quiz.question: What does Moore's Law predict?
options: Transistor counts double roughly every two years
